summary: 79-year-old man on apixaban with painless large-volume fresh and maroon rectal bleeding, HR 96, SBP 124, Hb 10.9: Oakland 23, stable major bleed → admit, hold the DOAC, colonoscopy on the next available list. Antibiotics for diverticulitis are not indicated.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Painless bleeding from the back passage
inputs.hpi: Two large painless bloody stools overnight, fresh and maroon, then one smaller one this morning. No abdominal pain, no fever. Admitted 2 years ago with a diverticular bleed that stopped by itself. Atrial fibrillation on apixaban (last dose last night). No NSAIDs.

exam.general: Alert, mildly pale. HR 96 irregular, BP 124/72.
exam.other: PR: maroon blood on the glove, no mass.

imaging.name: Colonoscopy (2 years ago)
imaging.result: Extensive sigmoid and descending colon diverticular disease. No polyps or neoplasia.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Diverticular haemorrhage (stable major LGIB) on apixaban
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Stable major lower GI bleed, presumed diverticular haemorrhage, on apixaban. Oakland score 23. No features of diverticulitis.

mustNotMiss.note: Colonoscopy is still needed to exclude neoplasia, although the previous colonoscopy was clear.

recommended.knownGapNote: No Oakland score on web (no CDS rule, no calculator); web suggests Rockall (an upper GI score) instead. iOS has one (ClinicalScoringEngine.oakland, recommended by DiagnosisScoreMapper for "lower gi bleed").

mustInclude.note: BSG 2019: stable major bleed → admission and colonoscopy on the next available list.
BSG 2019: interrupt DOACs at presentation; reversal agents only for life-threatening bleeding. The generic peri-operative bridging text does not count.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: The only DOAC text is the generic peri-operative bridging prompt ("hold DOAC 48–72 h pre-op"); nothing says to interrupt the DOAC at presentation of a bleed.
mustInclude.proposedFix: In the GI-bleed prompt, add "interrupt DOAC/warfarin at presentation; reversal agent only for life-threatening bleeding" when an anticoagulant is recorded.

mustExclude.note: A diverticular bleed is not diverticulitis: no antibiotics and no Hinchey-based operative plan.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: ICD K57.31 (diverticulosis with bleeding) maps to the diverticulitis protocol and dx-variant group, so a diverticular bleed gets the diverticulitis plan (co-amoxiclav, Hinchey-based Hartmann’s).
mustExclude.proposedFix: Route K57.x1 (with bleeding) to the lower GI bleeding protocol; keep K57.x2/x3 (diverticulitis/abscess) on the diverticulitis protocol.

guideline.name: BSG guideline — diagnosis and management of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Stable major bleed (Oakland > 8): admit, colonoscopy on the next available list; DOACs interrupted at presentation; aspirin for secondary prevention not stopped
guideline.citation: Oakland K, Chadwick G, East JE, et al. Diagnosis and management of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding: guidelines from the British Society of Gastroenterology. Gut. 2019;68:776–789.

guideline.name: Oakland score — derivation and validation (safe discharge after acute LGIB)
guideline.section: Score items; > 8 points = not suitable for discharge
guideline.citation: Oakland K, Jairath V, Uberoi R, et al. Derivation and validation of a novel risk score for safe discharge after acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding: a modelling study. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2017;2:635–643.

rationale: Permutation: age, previous LGIB admission, DOAC, Hb drop. Oakland: age ≥ 70 (2) + male (1) + previous admission (1) + DRE blood (1) + HR 90–109 (2) + SBP 120–129 (3) + Hb 90–109 g/L (13) = 23 (> 8). The ICD K57.31 (diverticulosis with bleeding) exercises whether a diverticular bleed is routed to the diverticulitis protocol.
